text:
Record each user’s HR@10 hit indicator for every coefficient and baseline. For a paired, dataset-stratified bootstrap, independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical sampled indices across methods; retain each user’s fixed candidates. Across roughly 10,000 replicates, compute category differences and their equal-weight macro average; report 95% intervals, observed gains, and discordant hit counts. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Pairing preserves within-user dependence ([SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)).

Choosing the best of four coefficients separately per dataset introduces selection optimism: validation noise helps determine each winner. Repeated architecture, seed, or coefficient searches increase reuse beyond these four choices. Report all coefficients’ scores, selection rules, and search history. Bootstrap reselection frequencies can describe instability; estimating optimism requires separating selection from assessment within a diagnostic resampling procedure. Such estimates remain approximate and should not replace the pinned benchmark score. Recomputing winners and evaluating them on the same bootstrap sample does not remove optimism ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

A conventional paired interval around the selected winner treats its coefficient as fixed; excluding zero does not establish valid post-selection significance. Prespecified simultaneous comparisons can address a declared finite comparison family, but not unrecorded adaptive searches. Describe small gains as exploratory until independently evaluated. User bootstrap intervals condition on trained models, four datasets, and fixed candidate sets: they omit training-seed and negative-sampling variability and do not establish full-catalog superiority. Sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings ([Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651)). These diagnostics require no hidden test labels or benchmark changes.
